Policy.Rule: Every current M-* module has exactly one derived V-M-* entry routed by VD-MAIN; evidence is current-state guidance and provenance, not a claim that historical commands were rerun.
Verification combines deterministic unit/contract tests, disposable PostgreSQL proof, fixture and no-legacy gates, XML validation, compose health, and runtime-final evidence.
Cross-channel access, immutable snapshot/run lifecycle, idempotency, retries, cancellation, retention, diagnostics, and stale-worker fencing must fail closed.
Coverage is reported per surface using metrics each tool emits; missing metrics stay explicit and never collapse into a fake repository-wide 100 percent claim.

For target coverage, complete means every declared invariant, API operation, removed-alias rule, user flow, worker step, channel recovery path, and diagnostic failure has explicit automated or runtime proof.
Never assert raw secrets, bot tokens, private object URLs, or full prompt payloads.

FailureTaxonomy.Failure: media_asset_invalid: unsupported, unreadable, oversized, unsafe, or incomplete input.
channel_account_mismatch: caller attempts cross-account read or mutation.
collection_version_conflict: mutable collection operation used a stale version.
selection_snapshot_invalid or selection_snapshot_not_sealed: unavailable/cross-account input or run creation from an unsealed snapshot.
stored_object_unavailable or stored_object_missing: retention/deletion/provider resolution removed required bytes or metadata/body state diverged.
analysis_prerequisite_missing, analysis_prerequisite_failed, analysis_prerequisite_unavailable: required transcript/text preparation is absent, failed, or unschedulable.
asr_runtime_unavailable, asr_invalid_audio, asr_unexpected_runtime_error, asr_empty_transcript, asr_request_timeout: stable CopperASR boundary failures without legacy fallback.
worker_failed: internal execution failed with durable diagnostic context.
artifact_unavailable: output is pending, failed, expired, deleted, or unpublished.
retention_denied, retention_delete_failed, retention_reconciled_orphan: lifecycle fence denial, bounded physical-delete retry, or managed-prefix reconciliation evidence.
export_provider_resolution_failed, export_retry_exhausted, export_delivery_failed: provider resolution, fenced retry, or adapter delivery failure.
workspace_cleanup_failed: scratch cleanup failed observably while terminal product state remains unchanged.

V-M-CONTRACTS.Summary: Contract schemas cover target vocabulary, envelopes, validation, scope, lifecycle, and fixture compatibility.

Scenarios.Scenario: Schema surfaces reject removed product vocabulary and preserve arrays for empty lists.
Target fixtures keep stable channel, object, selection, run, artifact, and diagnostic identities.

V-M-CONTRACTS.TraceAssertion: Contract tests assert canonical media_asset, stored_object, collection, selection_snapshot, analysis_run, artifact, diagnostic, channel_account, and operation_request names.

V-M-API-HTTP.Summary: Public and internal API routes enforce channel scope and expose ingestion, collection, selection, run, artifact, diagnostics, channel surfaces, and worker-step controls.

Scenarios.Scenario: Public envelopes preserve empty arrays, pagination bounds, idempotency, conflict mapping, and diagnostic access.
Internal worker routes claim, progress, cancel-check, and finalize only the scoped analysis_run_step.

V-M-API-HTTP.TraceAssertion: API tests assert cross-channel denial before storage mutation and stable diagnostic codes for invalid operations.

V-M-API-DOMAIN.Summary: Domain rules preserve immutable snapshots, channel-account isolation, prerequisite planning, cooperative cancellation, retention, and diagnostic lineage.

Scenarios.Scenario: Processing launch captures exact collection membership, seals a selection_snapshot, creates run steps, pins sources, and leaves later arrivals live.
Reusable transcript planning handles single-source reuse and mixed ordered inputs without mutating snapshots.
Cancel requested runs resolve late worker finalization as canceled.

V-M-API-DOMAIN.TraceAssertion: Target runtime tests assert diagnostics for missing, failed, and unavailable prerequisites and retention transitions.

V-M-API-STORAGE.Summary: Target PostgreSQL repositories and migrations persist API-owned product state with idempotency, optimistic versions, lineage, and channel-surface uniqueness.

Scenarios.Scenario: Disposable PostgreSQL migration is applied twice and target repositories prove operation/run idempotency replay, collection conflicts, immutable snapshots, lifecycle events, artifacts, diagnostics, retention, and surface supersede history.

V-M-API-STORAGE.TraceAssertion: Storage tests assert channel-account predicates on product reads and writes, optimistic-version conflicts, immutable snapshot behavior, and the queue-specific token checks that are currently implemented.

V-M-API-STEP-CONTROL.Summary: Internal worker-step control provides claim-once transition, progress recording, cancel checks, and finalization. Lease expiry and per-attempt-token stale-worker fencing are not implemented and remain tracked by media-j1qu.

Scenarios.Scenario: A queued step can be claimed with an owner, its progress can be recorded, cancel-check exposes cooperative cancellation, and finalization updates the owning run.
Current tests do not prove expiry or reassigned-attempt rejection; those assertions remain pending until media-j1qu is implemented.

V-M-API-STEP-CONTROL.TraceAssertion: Step-control tests cover claim results, progress events, cancellation checks, valid finalization, missing steps, invalid outcomes, and storage failures; they do not assert lease-expiry or attempt-token fencing.

V-M-API-EVENTS.Summary: Run, collection, artifact, diagnostic, and polling/live-update events provide restart-safe lifecycle visibility.

Scenarios.Scenario: Lifecycle changes emit ordered, channel-scoped events that adapters can poll or subscribe to without owning product state.

V-M-API-EVENTS.TraceAssertion: Event evidence remains a runtime-proof-pending boundary until the live event path is exercised.

V-M-INTERACTION-SURFACES.Summary: Channel surfaces, subjects, and events preserve external presentation mappings, active uniqueness, supersession, and restart recovery.

Scenarios.Scenario: Repeated upsert returns the persisted surface, primary subject uniqueness holds, stale surfaces supersede safely, and active surfaces recover after restart.

V-M-INTERACTION-SURFACES.TraceAssertion: Surface tests assert presentation mutations cannot alter media_asset, collection, snapshot, or run lifecycle.

V-M-WORKER-COMMON.Summary: Shared worker transport, source materialization, object-store safety, CopperASR response normalization, and document rendering remain deterministic.

Scenarios.Scenario: Worker API parsing accepts sealed selection metadata and rejects malformed or cross-scope payloads.
Object-store keys stay bucket-relative and path-safe; provider transport maps stable failures without fallback.

V-M-WORKER-COMMON.TraceAssertion: Focused worker-common tests assert bounded object keys, deterministic document outputs, and CopperASR diagnostic normalization.

V-M-WORKER-TRANSCRIPTION.Summary: Transcription worker processes text, documents, reusable transcript artifacts, and CopperASR speech inputs in selection order, then publishes policy artifacts.

Scenarios.Scenario: Text-only selections produce ordered transcript artifacts without ASR; mixed selections include inline/object text and reuse ready transcript artifacts while ASR handles only missing speech.
Provider failures become asr_* diagnostics; cancellation and missing artifacts fail closed.

V-M-WORKER-TRANSCRIPTION.TraceAssertion: Worker tests assert transcript_plain, transcript_segmented_markdown, transcript_docx, run_manifest, and run_diagnostics publication through API-owned artifacts.

V-M-COPPER-ASR.Summary: Pinned CopperASR runtime exposes health and transcribe endpoints with bounded CPU/thread configuration and no legacy ASR path.

Scenarios.Scenario: Runtime configuration and transport normalize successful, malformed, provider-error, and transport-error responses into stable TranscriptResult outcomes.
Compose health and no-legacy gates reject missing runtime, forbidden fallback, or stale Whisper references.

V-M-COPPER-ASR.TraceAssertion: CopperASR evidence proves the worker boundary and source pin; live long-voice performance remains a separate runtime gate.

V-M-WORKER-AGENT-RUNNER.Summary: Agent-runner consumes declared transcript/text-corpus artifacts, executes configured report or research harnesses, and publishes outputs and diagnostics.

Scenarios.Scenario: Declared step inputs materialize prepared text without discovering or transcribing raw speech; report and deep-research outputs preserve partial diagnostics and cancellation.

V-M-WORKER-AGENT-RUNNER.TraceAssertion: Agent-runner tests assert request-access expiry, workspace sanitization, harness failure redaction, artifact publication, and lease release.

V-M-MEDIA-EXPORT.Summary: Media-export worker enforces immutable output profiles, source pins, retries, cancellation fencing, transient object cleanup, and delivery claims.

Scenarios.Scenario: YouTube audio/video and uploaded video-to-audio jobs retain immutable profiles across retry and deliver with correct MIME, filename, and Telegram presentation.
Cancellation races and stale workers cannot publish output or success-only presentation facts.

V-M-MEDIA-EXPORT.TraceAssertion: Export tests assert source pins remain through queued/active states and release on every terminal outcome.

V-M-METADATA-ENRICHMENT.Summary: Metadata enrichment worker handles allowlisted canonical YouTube references with idempotency, leases, bounded provider metadata, retry backoff, and stale-worker fencing.

Scenarios.Scenario: Canonical YouTube ingestion creates one account-scoped metadata job without provider network calls in API; worker claims, heartbeats, retries, and finalizes only with a valid attempt token.
Successful finalization sanitizes title, thumbnail URL, duration, and performer metadata without mutating sealed snapshots.

V-M-METADATA-ENRICHMENT.TraceAssertion: Metadata tests assert expired leases use bounded backoff and stale workers cannot overwrite current media display metadata.

V-M-WEB-UI.Summary: Web UI presents materials, ordered selection, run status, results, errors, downloads, and retention through API contracts without service-only metadata.

Scenarios.Scenario: Normal UI routes use human labels, preserve ordered selection and explicit launch, and render API diagnostics without raw service manifests.

V-M-WEB-UI.TraceAssertion: Web tests assert runtime configuration stays behind the API client and ordinary result surfaces remain provider-agnostic.

V-M-TELEGRAM-ADAPTER.Summary: Telegram adapter ingests media, manages inbox and selections, renders restart-safe cards, delivers artifacts, and localizes presentation only.

Commands.Command: uv run --project apps/telegram-bot --with pytest --with pytest-asyncio pytest apps/telegram-bot/tests -q

Scenarios.Scenario: Telegram upload materializes channel-account media and inbox membership; explicit run action detaches captured membership while preserving later arrivals.
Current materials and terminal result surfaces recover after restart; duplicate user input can explicitly resend reusable transcript.

V-M-TELEGRAM-ADAPTER.TraceAssertion: Adapter tests assert provider-agnostic normal copy, stable callback vocabulary, localized presentation, and fenced delivery deduplication.

V-M-MCP-ADAPTER.Summary: MCP tools create/list media, seal selections, create runs, query diagnostics, and expose explicit artifact previews over the shared API.

Commands.Command: node --test --experimental-strip-types tests/api-client.test.ts tests/index.test.ts tests/protocol.test.ts tests/runtime.test.ts tests/tool-registry.test.ts

Scenarios.Scenario: MCP callers use channel-account-scoped contracts and can explicitly request run_manifest/provider metadata while normal adapters remain provider-agnostic.
Diagnostics and artifact download access preserve cross-channel denial and API-owned history.

V-M-MCP-ADAPTER.TraceAssertion: MCP tests assert tool registry, protocol envelopes, API client error mapping, and explicit artifact preview behavior.
